name: Judiciary

levels.note: 12th pass + typing. Age 18-27. Computer certificate preferred.
LLB degree. Age 21-35. PCS(J) exam by state PSC.
LLM or 7 years practice. Age 35-45. Higher Judicial Service exam.

stages.name: Preliminary Exam
stages.tests: 100-150 Qs — Law (Civil/Criminal/Constitutional), GK, English. Objective type.
stages.note: Qualifying. Cut-off varies by state and category.

stages.name: Main Exam (Written)
stages.tests: 3-4 papers: Civil Law, Criminal Law, English, Language (Hindi/Regional). Descriptive.
stages.note: Merit prepared from Main score. 3 hrs per paper.

stages.name: Interview
stages.tests: 20-30 min panel. Legal knowledge, personality, aptitude for judicial service.

stages.name: Training & Posting
stages.tests: 6-12 months judicial training at state judicial academy.
stages.note: Posted as Civil Judge / Judicial Magistrate after training.

reality: Judicial service exams are state-specific. Each state has its own syllabus and pattern.
PCS(J) is one of the most competitive exams. 10,000+ applicants for 100-200 vacancies.
Law degree (LLB) is mandatory. 3-year or 5-year LLB both accepted.
Some states require 2-3 years of practice for HJS (Higher Judicial Service).
Judges have job security but heavy workload. 50-100 cases per day in trial courts.
Salary: Civil Judge ~₹77,840 (Level 10) + DA + HRA. District Judge ~₹1,44,840 (Level 12).

syllabus.pattern: 100-150 Qs — Civil Law, Criminal Law, Constitutional Law, CPC, CrPC, Evidence Act, Contract Act, Transfer of Property. GK + English.
syllabus.books: PCS(J) Guide (Amazon) · Flipkart

syllabus.pattern: 3-4 papers (descriptive) — Civil Law (CPC, Contract, TPA), Criminal Law (IPC, CrPC, Evidence), English (Essay + Translation), Hindi/Regional Language.
syllabus.books: Judicial Services Mains Guide (Amazon)

syllabus.pattern: 20-30 min — Legal knowledge, personality, aptitude for judicial service. 200 marks.

faq.q: What is PCS(J) and how is it different from UPSC?
faq.a: PCS(J) = Provincial Civil Service (Judicial). State-level exam for Civil Judge posts. UPSC conducts exams for central services (IAS, IPS). Different eligibility, syllabus, and recruiting body.

faq.q: Can a 3-year LLB graduate apply for judicial service?
faq.a: Yes. 3-year LLB after graduation or 5-year integrated LLB both accepted. Some states require minimum age 21-22 and maximum 35.

faq.q: Is practice experience required for judicial service?
faq.a: For lower judiciary (Civil Judge): no experience required in most states. For higher judiciary (District Judge): 7 years practice required. Check state-specific rules.

faq.q: What is the age limit for judicial service exams?
faq.a: Civil Judge: 21-35 years (varies by state). District Judge: 35-45 years. Age relaxations for SC/ST/OBC/PwD.

faq.q: How many vacancies are there in judiciary?
faq.a: UP: 100-200 (Civil Judge) annually. Bihar: 100-150. Total judicial vacancies exceed 2000 per year across India. High Courts recruit separately.

faq.q: Where do I find official judiciary notifications?
faq.a: State PSC websites (uppsc.up.nic.in, bpsc.bihar.gov.in) and High Court websites. SarkariJobs+ links the official notification on every listing.
